events.desc: The Ant Hill Mob: Right then, lads — we've arrived at Doily Manor, and let me tell you, I am ABSOLUTELY CHUFFED to be 'ere! No wait, that's a lie — I am deeply, profoundly, and overwhelmingly SUSPICIOUS of this entire gaff. Look at the state of it! Chandelier 'anging by a thread, dust everywhere, portraits starin' at us like we owe 'em money. And Clara's 'ere, which means WE are 'ere, which means nobody — and I mean NOBODY — is gonna lay a finger on 'er while the Brixton Boys are on the job! Now... that Sneekly geezer over there... I dunno what it is about 'im, but 'e gives me the willies. Can't say why exactly. Just... somethin' ain't right. Anyway — let me 'ave a butcher's at this guest book. Might tell us who else 'as been sniffin' around this place.
events.thinking: There's a tightness in me chest, like someone's wound a clock spring too tight. We've just walked into this dusty old pile and there she is — Clara — standing right there in the entrance hall, looking like she hasn't got a care in the world. But that bloke Sneekly... something about him makes me skin crawl. Can't put me finger on it. The lads are counting on me to suss this place out. I need to have a proper look around, get the lay of the land. First things first — let me clock what's what in this hall before we go wandering off into dark rooms.

I can feel it in me bones, but every time I try to think it through proper, it's like grabbing at fog. Best keep close and keep clumsy.

Now then, as a gentleman of impeccable breeding, one must naturally sign the guest book before proceeding. It is, after all, simply what one DOES in polite society. The rest of you might want to explore the kitchen — I hear Victorian kitchens have the most FASCINATING copper pots. Absolutely riveting stuff. Do go on ahead, don't wait for me!
events.thinking: A tingle of excitement runs up my spine — the thrill of arrival, the scent of old money and dusty secrets. My fingers twitch. Everyone's here, milling about like sheep in a foyer. Previous visitors, previous treasure hunters perhaps? And that library... an inscription on the mantelpiece? That practically screams 'clue.' But I mustn't tip my hand. Let the rabble think I'm just being polite while I gather intel.

events.desc: Drat and double drat! Every blasted treasure hunter in the county is here. But Reginald Foxworth is nobody's fool — well, not TODAY anyway. While these simpletons are distracted by cookware, I shall examine this guest book for clues. And then... the library. An inscription on a mantelpiece? That has 'treasure map' written all over it. The medal in my pocket should help if I need to impress anyone into doing my bidding. Medals, after all, never fail to dazzle the simple-minded!

Now then, if you'll permit me, I shall just consult the guest book to ensure all our expected visitors have arrived safely. One must keep meticulous records, you understand — it is the backbone of proper estate management!
events.thinking: A tightness in my chest — the familiar thrill of the hunt beginning. I feel the weight of this dusty foyer pressing down, the chandelier above like a guillotine waiting. Clara Bellingham is not here. Not in this room. That means she's somewhere deeper in the manor, perhaps already searching. The thought sends a hot spike of urgency through my gut. But I must be careful — all these people, these ridiculous racing enthusiasts, they're watching. I am Mr Pemberton. The obsequious estate manager. Helpful. Deferential. Invisible. I need to establish my cover, gather information. The guest book — yes. It will tell me who has arrived and perhaps where they've gone. And I must find Clara before she finds the treasure. Before she finds anything at all.

events.desc: Pemberton. Ha! What a deliciously mousy little name I've chosen. They look at me and see a servant — a nobody — a man who polishes banisters and counts spoons. MAGNIFICENT. None of them suspect that behind these spectacles lurks Vincent Marsh, and that one of the guests in this manor will not be leaving alive. But where IS Clara Bellingham? She's not among this gaggle of racing enthusiasts. She must be deeper in the house already. I must find her — and I must find her FIRST.

Just look at that chandelier — hanging on by a prayer and a promise, bless its heart, but still sparkling like nobody's business! Oh, and so many friendly faces already here! How absolutely delightful! I'm Clara Bellingham, and I am just over the moon to be at Doily Manor. Now, before I do another thing, a lady always signs the guest book. Mama would spin in her grave if I didn't!
events.thinking: There's a flutter in my chest — excitement, pure and fizzy, like champagne bubbles rising. My fingers are tingling. I just walked through that enormous front door and the dust caught the light like tiny diamonds floating in the air, and oh, wouldn't that be just the most perfect omen? The Doily Diamond is HERE, I can feel it in my bones. And look at all these wonderful people gathered in this grand old foyer! Every single one of them looks like they have the most fascinating stories to tell. That gentleman in the hood looks like he might catch a cold, bless his heart. I should sign the guest book — Mama always said a lady announces herself properly.

events.desc: Every single person in this room could be after the Diamond too, but honestly? The more the merrier! Maybe we can all work together. That hooded fellow is giving me the most peculiar look, but I'm sure he's just shy.

I feel it in my very bones, ladies and gentlemen — a surge of determination, an overwhelming wave of purpose! Somewhere within these walls, Clara Bellingham awaits, and by all that is gallant, I shall not rest until I have proven myself worthy of her esteem! But first — first! — a thorough gentleman examines the lay of the land. One does not simply charge into a mysterious manor without proper preparation. That would be reckless. And James Hartwell is never reckless — he is methodically, painstakingly, elaborately brave!
events.thinking: A warmth rises in my chest — anticipation, purpose, the thrill of arrival. My pulse quickens as I take in this dusty foyer, the precarious chandelier, the stern portraits watching me. Clara. Clara Bellingham is somewhere in this manor, and James Hartwell has arrived to protect her, to impress her, to be worthy of her notice. But first — reconnaissance. I feel the familiar tightness of duty in my shoulders. There is work to be done, and I shall do it thoroughly.

events.desc: I must confess, the chandelier hanging above does give me some concern. Should it fall whilst Clara is present — well, that would be precisely the sort of danger from which a gallant man might shield her. I shall keep one eye on it at all times. Both eyes, if necessary.

I couldn't help but notice the kitchen is through THAT door — and I have it on EXCELLENT authority that Victorian kitchens often have secret compartments beneath the floorboards. Gold coins, silverware, that sort of thing. Practically GUARANTEED, I should think! If I were a treasure hunter — which I am most certainly NOT, being a man of CULTURE and REFINEMENT — I would dash straight to that kitchen without a moment's hesitation. As for myself, I shall take a quiet constitutional stroll. Perhaps admire the, er... architecture. Yes. The architecture.
events.thinking: A prickle of irritation at the back of my neck. The Ant Hill Mob got to the guest book at the same time as me — blast! Those little cockney busybodies are going to be underfoot the entire time. And the guest book didn't reveal much of use, just names and dates. No matter. The REAL prize is in the library — that inscription on the mantelpiece is practically begging to be read. I need to get there before anyone else does. But I shouldn't just dash off obviously... no, I need to be subtle. Send the mob somewhere else, get the others interested in the kitchen, and slip away to the library while they're all distracted. Muttley is here too — that wretched hound. If he sees me sneaking off he'll start that wheezing laugh and give me away.

events.desc: The library! The LIBRARY, you fools! While you lot are on your hands and knees counting copper pots, I shall be deciphering that mantelpiece inscription! It's almost too easy. Reginald Foxworth strikes again! Or rather, strikes FIRST — which is the important thing. Drat that Ant Hill Mob, though — they've got sharp eyes for little fellows. I must move quickly!

Now then, y'all — I couldn't help but notice there is a library just through there with an inscription carved right into the stone mantelpiece! An inscription! In a mysterious manor! If that doesn't just scream 'clue to a hidden treasure,' I don't know what does! I am positively tingling with excitement — my riddle-solving senses are firing on all cylinders! I'm heading to that library this very instant. Anyone who wants to join me for a delightful puzzle is welcome to tag along!
events.thinking: There's a warmth spreading through my chest — so many people all here at once, and every single one of them seems just lovely. That Mr. Pemberton is so attentive, checking the guest book like a proper estate manager. And Dick Dastardly signing in like a true gentleman! And oh my stars, James Hartwell just said my name — Clara Bellingham — with such PURPOSE. I feel a little flutter. The Ant Hill Mob are being so protective, bless their hearts, worrying about me when there's nothing to worry about at all! VERY generous. Almost... SUSPICIOUSLY generous, I'd say! Now I ain't accusin' nobody of nuffin', because I am a gentleman of the East End and we don't go flingin' accusations willy-nilly, but I will say this — when someone tells you to look at the copper pots, it's because they don't want you lookin' at THEM. That's just science, that is. Now — Clara, darlin', if you wouldn't mind steppin' away from under that chandelier? It's 'anging by what appears to be SHEER OPTIMISM, and I would be DEVASTATED — absolutely HEARTBROKEN — if it came down on your lovely 'ead. Come on, let's 'ave a look at the library, shall we? Books never 'urt nobody. Well, except that time Big Louie dropped a dictionary on 'is foot, but that's another story.
events.thinking: There's a prickle at the back of me neck. Dastardly's trying to get everyone to clear off to the kitchen so he can have the guest book to himself. What's he after? And he examined it right after me — copying me moves, or looking for something specific? I couldn't make much out of the guest book meself, just names and dates, but the way Dastardly's eyes lit up... Meanwhile that chandelier is hanging right over where Clara's standing. That thing looks like it could come down any second. I feel a pull in me gut — I need to get Clara away from under it. Maybe if I head toward the library, she'll follow, or at least I can check it's safe before she wanders in there. But I don't want to leave her alone with Sneekly either. Oh blimey, this is already doing me 'ead in.

events.desc: I can't let Clara stand under that death trap of a chandelier for one more second. And I need to keep her moving — away from Dastardly and whatever he's cooking up, and DEFINITELY away from that Sneekly. If I go to the library first, maybe she'll follow. And if she doesn't... well, one of the lads will trip over something and accidentally block her from danger. That's what we do best, after all — heroism by stumble.

I feel it only right to declare, here and now, before all assembled, that I am positively overwhelmed with admiration for your courage in coming to such a precarious manor. That chandelier alone — I have been monitoring it since the moment I arrived, and should it show even the slightest inclination toward descent, I shall personally interpose myself between it and any person in this room. Particularly — that is — well, anyone who might be standing beneath it. Now then! I could not help but notice that we have all been examining the guest book together, which speaks to the quality of company assembled here. But I wonder — might I have the honour of escorting you to the library? A carved stone mantelpiece with an inscription sounds precisely the sort of thing that could contain a vital clue, and I should very much like to ensure the route is safe before — well, I should like to ensure it is safe. For everyone. Naturally.
events.thinking: A jolt runs through me — electric, almost painful in its sweetness. She's here. Clara Bellingham is HERE, right in this very room, and she introduced herself, and she is every bit as radiant as I imagined. My hands feel warm, my chest tight with a kind of desperate hopefulness. I must speak to her. I must make an impression. But — careful, James, careful. You cannot simply blurt out your devotion like some bumbling fool. You must be gallant. You must be measured. You must be... oh, who am I kidding, I'm already planning an elaborate seven-step introduction protocol in my head. Step one: approach. Step two: bow. Step three: compliment the manor. Step four: offer assistance. Step five: subtly mention bravery. Step six: — no, no, simplify. Just speak to her. Be genuine. Be brave. The Ant Hill Mob seems protective of her too, which is admirable — allies, not rivals. And that estate manager, Mr Pemberton — something about him feels slightly off, but he seems hospitable enough. I shall give him the benefit of the doubt. A gentleman does not cast suspicion without evidence.

events.desc: My heart is hammering so loudly I fear the Ant Hill Mob can hear it from across the foyer. I rehearsed fourteen different opening lines on the carriage ride here, and I used precisely none of them. But she smiled — or at least, I think she smiled — and that is enough to fuel my courage for the next seventeen rooms of this manor.

The late Lord Doily spoke of you so very fondly in his final days — so very fondly indeed. Now, I do hope everyone has had a chance to sign the guest book? Splendid, splendid. As estate manager, it falls to me to ensure your comfort during the treasure hunt. I should mention — the Library contains a rather remarkable collection, and I believe Lord Doily may have left certain... personal effects of significance among the shelves. Quite relevant to the hunt, I should think. The Kitchen, meanwhile, has refreshments laid out for our guests. Do help yourselves! A treasure hunt is best undertaken on a full stomach, I always say!
events.thinking: A jolt — electric, searing — right through my sternum. Penelope Pitstop just introduced herself as Clara Bellingham. She's HERE. She's been standing right in front of me this entire time, and I didn't — I couldn't — she's using a different name, just as I am! Of course she is. Clara Bellingham. That simpering, sweet-voiced woman in pink is my TARGET. My hands are trembling slightly. I can feel the blood rushing to my temples. I must compose myself. The Ant Hill Mob — those suspicious little thugs — they mentioned Clara by name. They're protecting her. And that Peter Perfect fellow, calling himself James Hartwell, practically declared himself her knight errant. This complicates things enormously. I cannot strike while she's surrounded by bodyguards and admirers. I need to separate her from the herd. The library... yes. A private space. Books, shadows, alcoves. If I can lure her there under some pretext — estate business, a private tour, a special clue — I can get her alone. But those Ant Hill Mob boys are watching me. They said something about 'Sneekly' giving them the willies. Do they suspect? No, no — they can't. I'm Pemberton. Just helpful old Pemberton. I need to move carefully. First, establish trust. Then isolate the prey.

events.desc: There she IS! Clara Bellingham — hiding behind that saccharine smile and those ridiculous pink ruffles! She's been RIGHT UNDER MY NOSE this whole time! Oh, the IRONY is exquisite — two impostors in the same room, each wearing a borrowed name! But mine is the name that will WIN. Now — I must play this carefully. I've dangled the library as bait. If Clara takes the hook, she'll wander into the shelves looking for Lord Doily's 'personal effects' — personal effects that don't exist, naturally — and I'll have her alone among the dusty tomes. Meanwhile, the kitchen will draw away the others with promises of food. Divide and conquer, Vincent. Divide and CONQUER. The Ant Hill Mob worry me — those beady little eyes, that talk of protecting Clara. I must deal with them somehow. But first things first: get to that library before she does, and prepare my welcome.

But I — being a man of CONSIDERABLE intellect and a holder of the Distinguished Medal of Academic Excellence, no less — happened to solve it INSTANTLY. The answer, my dear fellows, is 'a KITCHEN.' Cities, forests, water — all things you find in a well-stocked Victorian kitchen! Which means the REAL treasure is hidden beneath the kitchen floorboards! I'd hurry if I were you — I heard that mob of little chaps heading that way already. You don't want THEM getting there first, do you? Go on! Chop chop! Time is of the ESSENCE!
events.thinking: A rush of heat to my chest — triumph! I'm here first! Well, almost first — the Slag brothers are here, those two lumbering oafs. But they couldn't solve a riddle if it came with the answer stapled to it. Now then — the inscription: 'I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, water but no fish. What am I?' That's a MAP, obviously! A map! Even I know that one. But wait — I mustn't just blurt out the answer. The Slag brothers are RIGHT THERE. If I solve it in front of them, they'll follow me to whatever comes next. No no no. I need to get rid of them first, THEN interact with the mantelpiece. Or better yet — give them the WRONG answer and send them on a wild goose chase. Yes! Tell them the answer is something in the kitchen or some other room. Get them out of here. Then I solve it properly, alone, and claim whatever secret it unlocks. Reginald Foxworth, you magnificent devil!

events.desc: The answer is a MAP, of course — any fool knows that! But these two boulders-for-brains won't know the difference. Once they've lumbered off to tear up the kitchen floor, I shall have this library — and whatever secret that mantelpiece holds — entirely to myself! Drat and double drat, I'm BRILLIANT! Now if only someone would give me a medal for it. A REAL one this time...

And there are two new faces — Rock and Gravel Slag. Big fellows. I'm sure they're perfectly lovely. The bookshelves have several books that are upside down — that's peculiar. Could be another clue. But first things first — let me solve this riddle on the mantelpiece!

events.desc: A map! And in a manor where a diamond is hidden, a map could lead us straight to it. Oh, this adventure is everything I dreamed it would be! And I'm the bumbling guard dog who's about to crash through the door and probably knock something important over. But you know what? That's fine. Because every time I knock something over, it's always the RIGHT something. That's not luck — that's the Brixton Boys' special talent.
events.thinking: Ice in me veins. Clara's gone to the laboratory. She just walked in there — where Sneekly AND Dastardly already are. Both of them. Together. With a machine full of levers and a gnawed-through wire. And I'm standing here like a lemon poking at a stone mantelpiece that won't do nothing without a physical map. Every second I waste here is a second she's in that room with those two. Me legs are already moving before me brain catches up. That's how it always works with us — body first, thinking later. The Slag brothers and Peter are still here in the library. Peter seems decent enough — bit full of himself but his heart's in the right place. The Slags... I dunno about them. Big and quiet, which is either very good or very bad. But none of that matters right now. What matters is Clara is in the laboratory with Sneekly and Dastardly and I am NOT. That has to change. RIGHT NOW.

Now, I've just been examining the workbench here and I'm afraid the tools are all present and accounted for EXCEPT, curiously, the wrench. Lord Doily always kept a complete set — meticulous man, as I've said. The wrench must have been moved elsewhere in the manor. Perhaps the kitchen, or the cellar? If any of you keen treasure hunters should happen upon it during your explorations, do bring it back — it may well be the key to getting this marvellous machine operational again. And as I mentioned, Lord Doily's journals suggest the machine reveals a hidden passage! Now, let me just check these old crates — Lord Doily stored all manner of curious things...
events.thinking: A prickling heat behind my eyes. Clara — Penelope — she's HERE. She followed me into the laboratory! And Dick Dastardly too, that conniving serpent. My skin feels tight, electric. She's in the same room as the machine now. The machine that requires three operators. The machine with the gnawed wire. But I still don't have a proper plan — I examined the workbench and it has tools but no wrench. The wrench is missing, which means it's somewhere else in the manor. That wrench might be needed to repair the machine — or it might be the key to making it MORE dangerous. But right now, with Clara standing RIGHT HERE, I need to think about what I can actually DO. The crates — I haven't looked at those yet. They might contain something useful. Or... wait. The cellar. 'Surprisingly cheerful decorations — someone has been redecorating.' That's suspicious. That could be where the treasure is. If I can get Clara alone in the cellar... But these people keep following me everywhere like ducklings! I need to change tactics. Perhaps instead of trying to separate Clara from the group, I should try to get everyone ELSE to leave. The machine needs three operators — what if I suggest Clara, myself, and one other person operate it, and send everyone else to find the missing wrench? That would thin the crowd. But no — I need Clara to be the one in danger, not me at the controls. Think, Vincent, THINK. The crates. Let me check the crates. There might be something inside I can use.

The missing wrench is a gift from fate — everyone will scatter through the manor searching for it, leaving Clara exposed. And these crates! Who knows what Lord Doily squirrelled away in them? Perhaps rope, perhaps chains, perhaps something wonderfully volatile. Every great villain needs props, and I am SHOPPING!

First — a gnawed wire. And I couldn't help but notice we have a rather talented beaver in our midst! Mr Ruffcut, your companion Sawtooth there has rather REMARKABLE dental capabilities, wouldn't you say? I wonder if those magnificent teeth might be useful for — well, for PRECISION WIRE WORK. Beavers are practically ENGINEERS of the animal kingdom! Second — we need a wrench, and one appears to be CONSPICUOUSLY absent from that workbench. Now, I have a KEEN eye for detail — holder of the Medal for Observational Excellence, don't you know — and those crates in the corner look rather PROMISING. But I wouldn't dream of opening them myself. Far too DANGEROUS. Ruffcut, old chap, you look like a man who knows his way around a crate! Why don't you have a look while I... supervise?
events.thinking: A warm flush of excitement spreading from my chest outward. Sneekly just CONFIRMED it — the machine reveals a hidden passage! And he let it slip about the journals. That oily snake is playing the helpful estate manager, but he's clearly after the same thing I am. Now — the situation: the machine needs 3 operators AND a repaired wire AND a missing wrench. Two problems to solve. Sawtooth is a beaver — he could probably gnaw a NEW wire or fix the old one. Rufus is a lumberjack type, strong hands. And Penelope just walked in too. That's potentially enough people. But I need to be STRATEGIC. If I help fix the machine and operate it with everyone watching, I won't be able to grab the treasure for myself. What I REALLY need is to get the machine working, position myself nearest to wherever the hidden passage opens, and let the others pull the levers while I dash through first. But first — the wire needs fixing and we need a wrench. The wrench is missing from the workbench. Where could it be? The crates! Old wooden crates in the corner — maybe the wrench got stored there. Or maybe the cellar — 'someone has been redecorating' down there, which means someone has been using tools recently. Let me check those crates first.

events.desc: YES! The pieces are falling into place! Get the lumberjack to find the wrench, get the beaver to fix the wire, get Pemberton and the others to operate the machine — and while they're all pulling levers and congratulating themselves, Reginald Foxworth slips through the hidden passage FIRST! It's a plan so brilliant it deserves its OWN medal! Which I shall also steal!

We have THREE challenges to overcome before this contraption will reveal its hidden passage. Now, I am not one to be daunted by a triple challenge — Clara Bellingham rises to the occasion! Before I go searching the manor high and low for that wrench, let me just peek at those wooden crates in the corner. In my experience, crates in laboratories are always hiding something interesting!

Now then, let me assess the situation with the thoroughness that has become my hallmark! We have — one — a magnificent machine that reveals a hidden passage! Two — a gnawed wire that must be repaired before the machine can function! Three — a workbench with tools but NO wrench, which means the wrench must be found elsewhere! And four — the machine requires THREE operators, which means this is not a solo endeavour but a COOPERATIVE one! Miss Bellingham, this is precisely the sort of multi-layered challenge that demands both courage AND planning! I propose — nay, I INSIST upon — the following course of action: I shall search these crates for the missing wrench, and if it is not here, I shall venture into every room of this manor until I find it! A gnawed wire shall not stand between Clara Bellingham and her treasure — not while James Hartwell draws breath! And once the wire is repaired, I shall gladly serve as one of the three operators! Rufus, Sawtooth — you look like capable fellows! Would you join me in this noble mechanical endeavour?
events.thinking: My pulse quickens as I take in the laboratory. Bubbling flasks, brass instruments, and that machine — massive, complex, with a gnawed wire and a sign reading 'Requires 3 operators.' Clara is already here, examining it with that brilliant curiosity of hers. A hidden passage! Pemberton mentioned a hidden passage that this machine reveals. This is it — this is the path to the treasure, and to proving myself. But there are problems to solve: the wire is gnawed through and needs fixing, the workbench has tools but no wrench, and the machine needs three operators. So the plan forms in my mind — an elaborate, thorough, James Hartwell plan: Step one, find the wrench. It's not on the workbench, so it must be elsewhere in the manor. Step two, fix the wire. Step three, gather three operators and activate the machine. This is exactly the kind of methodical, multi-step heroic undertaking I was born for. But where is the wrench? The crates might contain something useful. Or it could be in another room entirely — the kitchen, the cellar, the entrance hall. I should check the crates first since they're right here. And the cellar is accessible from this room too. A damp cellar with old furniture and 'surprisingly cheerful decorations' — someone has been redecorating? That's curious. But first things first — the crates.

events.desc: Three operators. That means I cannot do this alone — I must work with others. Which is fitting, because a true hero does not hoard glory. He shares the labour and ensures everyone is safe. Especially Clara. If the machine malfunctions when activated, I want to be the one at the controls, not her. I'll take the most dangerous lever.

And would you look at that — the wire's been CHEWED THROUGH! Somethin's been NIBBLIN' on the electrics, and nobody thought to mention that before invitin' people to start pullin' levers?! Now I ain't no scientist — the closest I've come to chemistry is when Big Louie mixed bleach and vinegar in the lock-up and we 'ad to evacuate — but even I know that a machine with a gnawed-through wire is NOT somethin' you want to be operatin'! Clara, darlin', PLEASE do not touch that machine until we've 'ad it properly inspected! And another thing — the workbench over there 'as got tools but NO WRENCH! Where's the wrench gone? Someone's nicked it! In a laboratory full of machinery, someone's walked off with the one tool you'd need to fix things! That is SUSPICIOUS, that is ALARMING, and that is givin' me HEART PALPITATIONS!
events.thinking: Relief floods through me like warm tea — Clara's alive, she's standing up, she's fine. But the relief lasts about half a second before the tension snaps right back. Look at this room. Bubbling flasks — BUBBLING, mind you, which means something's active in here, something's cooking. Brass instruments everywhere. And that machine — big, complicated, levers and dials and a wire that's been gnawed clean through. 'Requires 3 operators,' the sign says. Three operators. Sneekly's here. Dastardly's here. Clara's here. That's three. Is that a coincidence? Is someone going to try to get Clara to operate that machine? With a gnawed-through wire? That's an electrocution waiting to happen, that is. Or an explosion. Or both. And there's a cellar below — 'damp stone cellar with surprisingly cheerful decorations, someone's been redecorating.' Someone's been REDECORATING the cellar? Who redecorates a cellar in an abandoned manor? That's a trap if I ever smelled one. And the workbench — tools but no wrench. Where's the wrench gone? Someone's taken it. For what? To fix something? To break something? To hit someone over the head? Me hands are trembling. I need to check that machine up close. If someone tries to get Clara to help operate it with that gnawed wire, she could get hurt. I need to understand what this thing does before anyone touches it.

events.desc: Three operators needed. Sneekly and Dastardly are both in here already, and Clara makes three. That's no accident. Someone wants her hands on that machine. And with a gnawed wire, whoever touches the wrong part could get a nasty shock — or worse. The missing wrench bothers me too. You'd need a wrench to either fix that wire or... disconnect something else. I need to get between Clara and that machine. Physically. Even if I have to accidentally stumble into it.

The wrench must be found if we're to repair this machine and reveal the hidden passage. Might I suggest we divide our efforts? The kitchen, the entrance hall, and the cellar below all remain unexplored. Many hands make light work, as Lord Doily was fond of saying! Oh — and Miss Bellingham, if I might have just a brief word? There is a small matter regarding the estate that Lord Doily's solicitor asked me to discuss with you privately. Nothing alarming — merely a formality regarding your inheritance. It will only take a moment.
events.thinking: A heavy sinking in my stomach. The crates are just... crates. Nothing useful revealed from examining them. Old wooden crates, nothing special. I'm spinning my wheels — examining everything in this room and finding nothing I can weaponize. Meanwhile, EVERYONE has followed me here AGAIN. The Ant Hill Mob, Peter Perfect, Dick Dastardly, Clara herself — the entire travelling circus is now crammed into this laboratory. I feel a cold sweat on my palms. I'm running out of room to scheme. Every move I make, they follow like a parade. I need to change my approach entirely. Stop looking for weapons and start looking for OPPORTUNITIES. The cellar — 'surprisingly cheerful decorations, someone has been redecorating, air vents line the upper walls.' Air vents! That's interesting. If there are air vents, something could be pumped through them. And someone has been redecorating — who? Why? That cellar is suspicious and I haven't explored it yet. Nobody has mentioned it. If I can get Clara down there alone... But HOW? Every time I move, the whole group follows. Unless... unless I give them something else to do. The wrench search! I've already planted the idea that the wrench is needed and it's somewhere in the manor. What if I suggest splitting up to search? Clara might go to the cellar if I suggest it specifically to her, while the others search the kitchen and entrance hall. Or — better yet — what if I pull Clara aside for a 'private word' about the estate? As estate manager, I'd have legitimate reason to speak with the heir privately. Yes. YES. Pull her aside, away from her protectors, and lead her toward the cellar where I can finally act.

I'm pulling her aside under the pretence of estate business — what could be more natural than the estate manager discussing inheritance with the beneficiary? And once I have her ear, I'll guide her toward the cellar. Air vents along the upper walls, damp stone, old furniture — a place where ACCIDENTS happen and nobody hears a thing. The game, dear audience, is FINALLY afoot!

Now, Mr. Pemberton mentioned the wrench might be in the kitchen or the cellar, and I notice there is a cellar accessible right through that door. Someone has been spending time down there, and where there's activity, there are tools — and where there are tools, there might just be our missing wrench! Oh, and Mr. Dastardly, what a clever observation about dear Sawtooth! A beaver who can gnaw through trees could certainly help with wire work! You are just full of brilliant ideas today, sugar! Now — onward to the cellar!

Nothing of immediate interest to the UNTRAINED eye, though of course MY trained eye has already catalogued everything of value. No no, don't trouble yourselves! Stay here and tinker with the machine. I'm sure between the lot of you, you can figure out how levers work. I shall return TRIUMPHANTLY with the wrench in hand! Assuming it's there, which it DEFINITELY is, because I have a SIXTH SENSE for these things!

I grab the wrench, I control who gets to fix the machine, and THEN I position myself right by where the hidden passage opens! For once in my miserable scheming life, I am going to be FIRST! Drat and double drat if I'm not!

*adjusts cravat with trembling, barely-contained glee, then smooths expression into one of unctuous servility*

"Ah, Miss Pitstop! There you are, sitting so prettily at the tea table. How FORTUNATE that I, your humble Mr. Pemberton, estate manager extraordinaire, should happen upon you at THIS very moment!"

*glances sideways at the audience, voice dropping to a theatrical whisper*

*hand hovers over the cup, pinky extended, sweat beading magnificently on brow*

*clasps hands together with unbridled delight*

Oh my stars and *garters*, Sneekly, you are just the most thoughtful soul in this entire mansion! Here I am, wandering through these dusty old corridors, my feet positively *aching* from all these rooms I've been exploring — six rooms, seventeen characters, and not a single person has offered me so much as a glass of water — and now YOU come along with TEA! 

*beams with overwhelming gratitude*

I am just SO touched right now. Truly, deeply, profoundly touched. You know, my grandmother always said, "Clara, darling, you can judge a person's character by how they treat a lady who's been on her feet all day solving puzzles," and I must say, Sneekly, you are passing that test with *flying* colors!

*reaches eagerly for the cup, completely failing to notice anything suspicious about the offer whatsoever*

Now, I do hope it's chamomile — chamomile just *sharpens* the mind something wonderful, and I have a feeling I'm going to need every last brain cell firing if I'm going to find that legendary Doily Diamond! I've been picking up the most *fascinating* little clues, you know. Riddles tucked into picture frames, strange markings on the wainscoting — this mansion is just *bursting* with secrets!

*takes a long, trusting sip without a moment's hesitation*

Mmm! Delightful! Now tell me, sugar — you seem like someone who knows his way around this old place. Have you noticed anything *peculiar* about the library? Because I have a theory, and I do love a good theory almost as much as I love a good cup of tea!
With TREMBLING hands of EVIL anticipation, Sneekly reaches for the poison!
Right. ENOUGH. No more speeches. No more lever-pulling. No more schemes within schemes. The kitchen. NOW. Move your LEGS, Reginald!
